chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was the most beautiful of people in voice with the Quran, and the water carriers would pass by and stop at his door, listening to his recitation, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was the most beautiful of people in voice.
ai.seo_question: Who had the most beautiful voice for Quran recitation among the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi underscores the aesthetic and spiritual excellence of the Imams' Quranic recitation, highlighting Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) and Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) as paragons of vocal beauty. The detail of water carriers pausing to listen illustrates how their recitation transcended scholarly circles, serving as a public manifestation of divine eloquence that captivated even the working class. This aligns with the Shia tradition of valuing Tajweed and Melody (Maqamat) as means to deepen contemplation (Tadabbur) of the Divine Word.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hajjal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was of the most beautiful of voices of the people with the (recitation of the) Quran, and the water carriers used to pass by his<sup>asws</sup> door, and they would be pausing at his<sup>asws</sup> door listening to his<sup>asws</sup> recitation, and it was so that Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was of the most beautiful of voices of the people’.
en.sarwar: 11. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hajjal from Ali ibn ‘Aqabah from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was the best among the people for his attractive voice in reading the Holy Quran. The water carrier would stop in front of his door to listen to his reading and abu Ja’far (a.s.) was the best among the people for his attractive voice.”
